# Supplementary material {.appendix}

## Supplementary Methods

### S1. Development of the model {.unnumbered}

The final model is the third of three iterations. Each was critically evaluated, and the evaluation
determined the design of the next. They are summarised here because the comparisons
justify the design choices described in the main text.

**First iteration (v1; `code/`).** MaxEnt was fitted with background points drawn at random from all
land worldwide, with an arbitrary threshold of 0.5. Training AUC was
`r filter(v1v2, Metric == "Training AUC")$v1` with `r filter(v1v2, Metric == "Number of coefficients")$v1`
non-zero coefficients. The high AUC was largely an artefact of contrasting presences with distant,
environmentally irrelevant background [@barve2011].

**Second iteration (v2; `code_2/`).** The background was restricted to the accessible area and
corrected for sampling bias with a single global target-group surface. Predictors were chosen by
stepwise VIF reduction (BIO2, BIO3, BIO13, aridity, VPD), and the model was tuned by spatial-block
cross-validation (LQHP, β = 2). Block-CV AUC was `r fmt(as.numeric(filter(v1v2, Metric == "Test/Validation AUC")$v2))`.
When we tested transfer by withholding entire regions, however, the model failed:
LORO AUC was `r paste(sprintf("%s (%s)", fmt(v2_loro$auc), c("East Asia", "North America", "Oceania")[match(v2_loro$region, regs)]), collapse = ", ")`,
that is, at or below random (@suppfig-dev a). The future projections built on this model are
evaluated in S5.

**Diagnosis and redesign (v3; `code_3/optimisation/`).** Exploratory analyses isolated the causes.
(i) *Background.* With the v2 predictors and three MaxEnt configurations, replacing the v2 background
with a uniform or region-balanced target-group background raised mean LORO AUC from
`r fmt(mean(filter(opt_bg, bg == "bg_current")$loro_auc))` to `r fmt(mean(filter(opt_bg, bg == "bg_uniform")$loro_auc))`
and `r fmt(mean(filter(opt_bg, bg == "bg_regbias")$loro_auc))`, respectively (@supptbl-bg; @suppfig-dev b).
The v2 background placed most points in North America and, within regions, in the most heavily
sampled areas, so the model learned the sampling pattern. (ii) *Predictors.* Even with a corrected
background, the v2 predictor set had high transfer omission because it lacked an absolute temperature
gradient. This motivated the ten *a priori* sets described in the main text. (iii) *Algorithms.* On
the best single predictor set, MaxEnt was compared with a GLM with quadratic terms, a GAM, boosted
regression trees, a down-sampled random forest and three ensembles (@supptbl-alg; @suppfig-dev c).
MaxEnt had the best transfer calibration (LORO CBI = `r fmt(filter(opt_alg, model == "maxent")$loro_cbi)`)
and the lowest transfer omission (LORO OR10 = `r fmt(filter(opt_alg, model == "maxent")$loro_or10)`).
Random forests omitted most withheld records, and the ensembles did not improve on MaxEnt. (iv) *Consensus.* The
three top predictor sets performed similarly, so they were combined into the consensus used here
(`code_3`, and `code_6` for Australia).

```{r}
#| label: dev-figure-data
#| code-summary: "Show code: model development figure (new)"
dev_a <- bind_rows(
  v2_loro |> transmute(model = "v2 model", region = reg_lab[region], auc),
  kr6$cv_folds |> filter(scheme == "loro") |> transmute(model = "Final consensus", region = reg_lab[fold], auc)) |>
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = c("v2 model", "Final consensus")))
bg_lab <- c(bg_current = "v2 background", bg_uniform = "Uniform within M", bg_regbias = "Region-balanced target group")
dev_b <- opt_bg |> transmute(bg = factor(bg_lab[bg], levels = bg_lab), config = paste0(fc, ", β = ", rm),
                             `LORO AUC` = loro_auc, `LORO CBI` = loro_cbi, `LORO OR10` = loro_or10) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("LORO"), names_to = "metric")
alg_lab <- c(maxent = "MaxEnt", glm = "GLM", gam = "GAM", brt = "BRT", rf_down = "RF (down-sampled)",
             ens_all = "Ensemble (all)", ens_mx_gam_brt = "Ensemble (MaxEnt, GAM, BRT)", ens_mx_glm_gam = "Ensemble (MaxEnt, GLM, GAM)")
dev_c <- opt_alg |> transmute(model = factor(alg_lab[model], levels = rev(alg_lab)), `LORO AUC` = loro_auc, `LORO CBI` = loro_cbi,
                              `LORO OR10` = loro_or10, `Block AUC` = blk_auc, `Block OR10` = blk_or10) |>
  pivot_longer(-model, names_to = "metric")
```

### S2. Projection domain and relation to the Australia–New Zealand analyses {.unnumbered}

The analysis was first carried out for Australia and New Zealand together (`code_3`–`code_5`) and
then restricted to continental Australia and Tasmania (`code_6`–`code_8`). The calibration data,
background, predictor sets, tuning, consensus members, bootstrap seeds and threshold are identical in
both versions. Only the projection domain and the quantities that depend on it changed. Australian
results are therefore unchanged (@supptbl-domain). Three outputs differ by construction: the proportion
of known localities that remain suitable, which is now computed over Australian records only; the
gravity model, which now has two landmasses (mainland and Tasmania); and the surveillance allocation, in
which New Zealand no longer competes for visits. The New Zealand and Pacific results of the earlier
versions are not part of this paper.

### S3. Derivation of future predictors {.unnumbered}

Bioclimatic variables were computed from each GCM's monthly minimum and maximum temperature and
precipitation using the WorldClim definitions. Applied to current WorldClim 2.1 monthly climate, this
reproduces the training layers exactly (maximum difference < 10⁻⁵). The Thornthwaite aridity index was computed as
100 × the annual sum of monthly water deficits (PET − P in months with P < PET) divided by the sum of PET in those
months, with Hargreaves PET and extraterrestrial radiation by latitude and month. We computed
radiation directly with `envirem:::calcSolRad()`, because `envirem::ETsolradRasters()` (version 3.1)
assigns radiation by column rather than by row when used with `terra`. With correctly oriented
radiation our implementation reproduces `envirem::aridityIndexThornthwaite()` to within
`r formatC(kr7$envirem_check, format = "e", digits = 0)`. The index recomputed from WorldClim 2.1 is closely
correlated with the ENVIREM training layer (r = `r fmt(kr7$ai_cor, 3)`) but not identical, so future
change was applied as an anomaly to the training layer (@suppfig-validation a).

### S4. Lambda-based prediction {.unnumbered}

To make the 160 future projections, 4,800 bootstrap projections and the attribution analyses
tractable, predictions were computed directly from the fitted MaxEnt feature weights (lambdas) with
the cloglog transform and clamping. This reproduces the MaxEnt Java output to within
`r formatC(kr7$pred_check, format = "e", digits = 0)` and the current-climate map to within
`r formatC(kr7$cur_check, format = "e", digits = 0)`. Refitting the consensus from the stored inputs
reproduced the original models exactly (`r ifelse(isTRUE(kr7$refit_check), "verified", "not verified")`).

### S5. Re-evaluation of the earlier future-climate analysis {.unnumbered}

The earlier projection workflow (`code_2`, Steps 8–10) was reviewed line by line, its key calculations
were re-run, and the results were compared with the corrected analysis. Thirteen problems were
identified (@supptbl-v2). The most consequential was the derivation of future aridity, PET and CMI by
scaling current values with the ratio of future to current BIO1 in °C. Ratios of Celsius
temperatures have no physical meaning: the same 2 °C warming multiplies "PET" by 1.1 at 20 °C and by 21
at 0.1 °C. The resulting aridity exceeded its theoretical maximum of 100 in
`r fmt(filter(kr7$v2_ai_stats, grepl("MPI", id))$pct_above_100, 0)`% of Australian land under
MPI-ESM1-2-HR SSP2-4.5 2041–2060 and in `r fmt(filter(kr7$v2_ai_stats, grepl("ACCESS", id))$pct_above_100, 0)`%
under ACCESS-CM2 SSP5-8.5 2081–2100, reaching `r fmt(filter(kr7$v2_ai_stats, grepl("ACCESS", id))$max_v2, 0)`
(@suppfig-validation b). In the second scenario the mean increase in aridity was
`r fmt(filter(kr7$v2_ai_stats, grepl("ACCESS", id))$mean_change_v2, 1)` units under the v2 method but
`r fmt(filter(kr7$v2_ai_stats, grepl("ACCESS", id))$mean_change_v4, 1)` units when derived from the same GCM's
monthly climate, and `r fmt(filter(kr7$v2_ai_stats, grepl("ACCESS", id))$pct_outside_train_v2, 0)`% of cells lay
outside the calibration range (none with the corrected method).

### S6. Process-based model {.unnumbered}

Stage-specific lower developmental thresholds were taken from @yano1987 and thermal constants derived
from stage durations at 25 °C [@heath2016; @schappach2020] (@supptbl-procpar). Daily degree-days above
each threshold were calculated from monthly mean minimum and maximum temperature with the single-sine
method. The generation rate *G* is the reciprocal of the sum over stages of thermal constant divided by annual
degree-days. Desiccation was represented by the saturation deficit (SD) at the mean daily maximum
temperature, from WorldClim vapour pressure; in the future, vapour pressure was scaled with saturation
vapour pressure at the minimum temperature (constant relative humidity at dawn). A month was suitable
for larval questing if mean temperature exceeded the lowest developmental threshold and SD ≤ 10 mmHg.
Months with mean daily maximum ≥ 35 °C were heat-stress months, and months with SD > 20 mmHg (the
tolerance of nymphs and adults) were dry-stress months [@heath2016]. The index is
*P* = *f*~dev~(*G*) × *f*~moist~ × *f*~heat~ × *f*~dry~. Here *f*~dev~ rises linearly from 0 at *G* = 1/3 to 1 at
*G* ≥ 1, *f*~moist~ rises from 0 to 1 as larval-questing months go from 0 to 4, and *f*~heat~ and *f*~dry~ fall
from 1 to 0 as stress months go from 0 to 3. The nymph and adult questing season is the number of months with
mean temperature ≥ 10 °C and SD ≤ 20 mmHg. Two structural choices were made after inspecting a first
version: SD was evaluated at maximum rather than mean temperature, and the dry-stress term was added
because without it the model classified the semi-arid wheat–sheep zone as suitable. Both alternatives
are included in the sensitivity analysis (@supptbl-procval).

### S7. Gravity model and surveillance optimisation {.unnumbered}

Introduction pressure on unit *j* was *P*~*j*~ = Σ~*i*~ *C*~*i*~ (1 + *d*~*ij*~/*d*~0~)^−γ^ *s*~*ij*~, summed over
infested source units *i*. *C*~*i*~ is the number of cattle in the source, *d*~*ij*~ the great-circle distance,
*d*~0~ = 50 km and γ = 2, and *s*~*ij*~ = 1 within a landmass and 0.1 between mainland Australia and
Tasmania. Expected introductions were proportional to *P*~*j*~ × *C*~*j*~, and establishment risk was this
quantity multiplied by the fraction of the unit that is suitable, now or in 2041–2060 (SSP2-4.5,
weighted by GCM agreement). Candidate surveillance units were uninfested units that are at least 25%
suitable now or in 2041–2060. The prior probability that unit *j* harbours an undetected population was
*π*~*j*~ = 1 − exp(−*c R*~*j*~), with *c* chosen so that Σ*π*~*j*~ = *N*~0~. For a budget of *B* visits, the
allocation {*n*~*j*~} maximising 1 − Π~*j*~[1 − *π*~*j*~(1 − (1 − *p*)^*n*~*j*~^)] was found by greedy marginal
allocation. Greedy allocation is optimal here because each unit's contribution is concave in *n*~*j*~. The posterior
probability after *n*~*j*~ negative visits is *π*~*j*~(1 − *p*)^*n*~*j*~^ / [*π*~*j*~(1 − *p*)^*n*~*j*~^ + 1 − *π*~*j*~].

### S8. Global warming levels {.unnumbered}

The 20-year windows in which each CMIP6 simulation first reaches 1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 3 and 4 °C above
1850–1900 were taken from @hauser2022. For each GCM and SSP the warming level at the centre of each
period was interpolated between window centres. For periods after a simulation's last tabulated crossing
(for example SSP1-2.6 after warming stabilises), the warming level was estimated from a per-GCM linear
regression of warming level on projected mean warming over Australian land (@suppfig-gwlmap).

The equivalency test asks whether overlap is lower than expected if occurrences were interchangeable; the similarity test asks whether overlap is higher than expected given the climates available in the invaded range.

:::

```{r}
a3 <- kr3$area |> filter(!grepl("^NZ", jurisdiction))
e4 <- function(s, p) filter(kr4$ens_summ, unit == "Australia", ssp == s, period == p)$pct_change_med
e5c <- filter(kr5$expo_ens, group == "Cattle", unit == "Australia")$exposed_cur[1]
g5 <- filter(kr5$gwl_sum, unit == "Australia", gwl == 2)$med
sv5 <- function(j) { x <- filter(kr5$surv_jur, jur == j)$visits; if (length(x)) x else 0 }
tribble(~Quantity, ~`Australia + New Zealand (code_3–5)`, ~`Australia only (code_6–8)`,
  "Calibration records; consensus members", sprintf("%d; %s", kr3$n_occ, paste(kr3$sel_sets, collapse = ", ")), sprintf("%d; %s", kr6$n_occ, paste(kr6$sel_sets, collapse = ", ")),
  "Mean LORO AUC / CBI", sprintf("%s / %s", fmt(kr3$cv$loro_auc), fmt(kr3$cv$loro_cbi)), sprintf("%s / %s", fmt(kr6$cv$loro_auc), fmt(kr6$cv$loro_cbi)),
  "Threshold (cloglog)", fmt(kr3$thr_p10, 4), fmt(kr6$thr_p10, 4),
  "Suitable area in Australia now (10³ km²)", k3(sum(a3$suitable_km2), 1), k3(tot[["suitable"]], 1),
  "Change in Australia, SSP2-4.5 2041–2060 (%)", sgn(e4("245", "2041-2060"), 1), sgn(es("245", "2041-2060")$pct_change_med, 1),
  "Change in Australia, SSP3-7.0 2081–2100 (%)", sgn(e4("370", "2081-2100"), 1), sgn(es("370", "2081-2100")$pct_change_med, 1),
  "GCM share of variance, Australia, 2041–2060 (%)", fmt(100 * filter(kr4$vp, unit == "Australia", period == "2041-2060", component == "Climate model (GCM)")$frac, 1), fmt(vpv("2041-2060", "Climate model (GCM)"), 1),
  "Cattle in suitable climate in Australia now (M)", mil(e5c, 2), mil(ex_cur("Cattle"), 2),
  "Change in Australia at 2 °C (%)", sgn(g5, 1), sgn(gs(2)$med, 1),
  "Known localities suitable now (%)", paste(pct(kr4$known_cur), "(Australian and NZ records)"), paste(pct(kr7$known_cur), "(Australian records)"),
  "Surveillance visits (of 250): Victoria / Tasmania / NZ", sprintf("%d / %d / %d", sv5("Victoria"), sv5("Tasmania"), sv5("NZ South Island") + sv5("NZ North Island")), sprintf("%d / %d / –", sv("Victoria"), sv("Tasmania"))) |>
  kable()
```
Comparison of the Australia + New Zealand and Australia-only versions of the analysis. Calibration and the Australian projections are identical; the small difference in current suitable area is due to assigning the Jervis Bay Territory to New South Wales. Outputs that pool records or allocate effort across the domain differ by construction.
:::

```{r}
gcm_clim <- kr7$clim_all |> filter(domain == "Current suitable range") |>
  filter((ssp == "245" & period == "2041-2060") | (ssp == "585" & period == "2081-2100")) |>
  mutate(key = ifelse(ssp == "245", "a", "b")) |> dplyr::select(gcm, key, d_bio1, d_bio12_pct, d_aridity) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = key, values_from = c(d_bio1, d_bio12_pct, d_aridity))
kr7$gcm_meta |> left_join(gcm_clim, by = "gcm") |> arrange(!core, ecs) |>
  transmute(GCM = gcm, Centre = centre, `ECS (K)` = fmt(ecs, 1), Core = ifelse(core, "✓", ""), v2 = ifelse(v2, "✓", ""),
            `ΔT (°C), SSP2-4.5 2041–60` = fmt(d_bio1_a, 1), `ΔP (%), SSP2-4.5 2041–60` = fmt(d_bio12_pct_a, 0),
            `ΔT (°C), SSP5-8.5 2081–2100` = fmt(d_bio1_b, 1), `ΔP (%), SSP5-8.5 2081–2100` = fmt(d_bio12_pct_b, 0),
            `Δ aridity, SSP5-8.5 2081–2100` = fmt(d_aridity_b, 1)) |>
  kable(align = "llrccrrrrr")
```
Global climate models. ECS = equilibrium climate sensitivity [@meehl2020; @zelinka2020]. Climate changes are area-weighted means over the currently suitable range in Australia relative to 1970–2000. *Core*: ensemble used for all projections; *v2*: ensemble of the earlier analysis (UKESM1-0-LL and CNRM-CM6-1 used only in the sensitivity analysis).
:::
:::

::: {.supp-table}
::: {#supptbl-v2}
| # | Component | Earlier analysis (v2, `code_2` Steps 8–10) | Why it is a problem | This analysis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Model projected | v2 MaxEnt model (BIO2, BIO3, BIO13, aridity, VPD; stepwise VIF; LQHP). | Did not transfer between regions (LORO AUC `r paste(fmt(v2_loro$auc), collapse = ", ")`); warming entered only through proxies; it predicted `r fmt(v2_cur_area / 1e6, 2)` million km² currently suitable in Australia and New Zealand, `r fmt(v2_cur_area / kr3$tot[["suitable"]], 1)` times the area predicted by the validated model for the same domain. | Transfer-validated consensus with annual mean temperature in every member. |
| 2 | Future aridity, PET, CMI | Current ENVIREM values scaled by the ratio of future to current BIO1 (°C) and of future to current precipitation. | Ratios of Celsius temperatures are meaningless; aridity exceeded its maximum of 100 in `r fmt(min(kr7$v2_ai_stats$pct_above_100), 0)`–`r fmt(max(kr7$v2_ai_stats$pct_above_100), 0)`% of Australian land, producing most of the 60–81% extrapolation reported. | Aridity derived from each GCM's monthly climate with the ENVIREM formulation, applied as an anomaly (S3). |
| 3 | Future VPD | Current VPD × exp(0.06 ΔT). | Ignores changes in relative humidity, which differ among GCMs. | VPD not used in the consensus. |
| 4 | Baseline consistency | Change computed against one baseline applied to layers built on another. | Inconsistent anomalies. | Identical formulation for current and future WorldClim 2.1 monthly climate. |
| 5 | GCM ensemble | Five GCMs chosen without stated criteria; three with ECS > 4.5 K, one outside the very likely range. | Warm-biased ensemble [@hausfather2022]. | Ten GCMs screened for data, ECS and independence; v2 ensemble as a sensitivity analysis. |
| 6 | Scenario design | SSP2-4.5 and SSP5-8.5; 2041–2060 and 2081–2100. | No near-term period, no low-emission pathway; SSP5-8.5 the only high scenario [@hausfather2020]. | Four SSPs × four periods. |
| 7 | Suitable area | Cell count × a single cell area at the mean latitude. | Overestimated suitable area by `r fmt(100 * (kr7$area_v2_approx / kr7$area_true - 1), 0)`%. | True latitude-dependent cell areas. |
| 8 | Threshold | Maximum sensitivity + specificity. | Inconsistent with current-climate reporting. | 10th-percentile training presence; MSS as sensitivity. |
| 9 | Extrapolation | Univariate MESS only; statistics from unmasked maps. | Novel combinations and clamping ignored; inconsistent treatment. | MESS and ExDet NT2 for every scenario; clamped vs. unclamped. |
| 10 | Ensemble summary | Binary map of the median suitability; agreement for one scenario. | Area of the median map ≠ median of the areas. | Per-GCM binary maps; median and range of areas; agreement for every scenario. |
| 11 | Uncertainty | GCM spread only. | SDM uncertainty ignored [@buisson2010]. | Bootstrap × GCM × SSP; ANOVA partitioning. |
| 12 | Interpretation | No attribution; surveillance priorities from SSP5-8.5 2081–2100. | Drivers unknown; least policy-relevant scenario. | Temperature/moisture attribution; management categories for two focal scenarios. |
| 13 | Reproducibility | Hard-coded absolute paths; two MESS implementations. | Code did not run as written. | Relative paths; one validated MESS implementation. |

Problems identified in the earlier future-climate analysis and the corrections made. For comparison, the earlier analysis reported median changes of `r paste(sprintf("%+.0f%%", v2_unc$median_pct_change), collapse = ", ")` for SSP2-4.5 2041–2060, SSP2-4.5 2081–2100, SSP5-8.5 2041–2060 and SSP5-8.5 2081–2100 (Australia and New Zealand).
:::
:::

```{r}
#| fig-width: 13

p_da <- ggplot(dev_a, aes(region, auc, fill = model)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.75), width = 0.7) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey60", "#1b7837"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) sub(" \\(", "\n(", x)) + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Withheld region", y = "LORO AUC", tag = "a") + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
p_db <- ggplot(dev_b, aes(value, bg, colour = bg)) + geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 3, size = 4, colour = "black") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") + scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey50", "#4393c3", "#1b7837"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "b")
p_dc <- ggplot(filter(dev_c, metric %in% c("LORO AUC", "LORO CBI", "LORO OR10")), aes(value, model)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = model == "MaxEnt"), size = 2.4) + scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey40", "#1b7837"), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") + labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "c")
p_dev <- p_da + (p_db / p_dc) + plot_layout(widths = c(1, 2.2))
p_dev
save_fig("FigS1_model_development", p_dev, 13, 5)
```
Development of the model. (a) Transfer of the v2 model and of the final consensus to each withheld region (leave-one-region-out AUC; dashed line: random). (b) Effect of the background design on transfer, v2 predictor set; points are three MaxEnt configurations, crosses their mean. (c) Comparison of algorithms on one predictor set; MaxEnt in green. Lower OR10 is better (expected 0.10).
